notes: A complete fix with a tidy isUnquoted helper applied at every structural site, including the import mapping key, plus comprehensive tests (quote styles, {}, snippets, import block keys, unclosed blocks) and an adapt integration test.

A clean `Token.isUnquoted` helper is applied at all the same sites as the reference, including the import block-key check, with thorough parse, dispenser and adapt tests across quote styles and contexts.

Clean helper methods cover nearly every structural brace check, but it misses the `anonymous blocks are not supported` check in doImport, so a quoted "{" mapping key is still rejected; the tests are modest but relevant.

The helper methods are tidy, but it misses the `currentMappingKey == "{"` anonymous-block check in `doImport`, so a quoted `{` used as an import block key still errors; tests are reasonable but narrower.

A complete and correct fix using inline Quoted() checks, with redundant conditions removed and very thorough dispenser, parser and adapter tests across all quote styles; the tests are somewhat heavy and the exact-JSON adapter test is a bit brittle.
Uses `Quoted()` inline at every structural brace check and removes the redundant inner checks; tests are extensive across dispenser, parser, imported snippets and httpcaddyfile adaptation.
Covers every site the reference touches with inline wasQuoted checks, but the code is repetitive, leaves now-redundant inner quoted conditions in directive(), and adds only a single test case.

Adds inline `wasQuoted == 0` checks at every spot the reference touches, so the fix is complete, but it leaves now-redundant quoted checks inside the `{` and `{}` branches and adds only one table test case.

Its code is essentially the same as C1, with clean grouping by resource. It shares the gap that parent-module imports override all child imports for the resource instead of per instance. Good table tests cover for_each, count, import for_each and parent override.

This keeps every import block from the same module, so the reported for_each and count case is fixed, and the change is small; however, the parent-overrides-child rule still works per configuration resource, so a child-module import for a different instance than the parent targets is still silently dropped (the reference dedups per instance in expandResourceImports instead).

Fixes the reported same-module case by grouping all blocks per ConfigResource. However, a parent import still drops every child import for the whole resource rather than only the matching instance, so the same silent drop survives in mixed parent/child cases (consistent with 2/3 hidden tests failing). Its tests are thorough but encode that coarse semantics.

The code is the same as C1, a minimal per-resource grouping that fixes the reported bug but keeps the per-resource parent override; its new refactoring unit test explicitly asserts that the child's import of instance ["c"] is dropped, which locks in that same silent-drop behaviour.

Uses the same resource-level override, so a parent import for one instance still silently drops child imports for other instances. It also leaves FindImportStatements as a dead wrapper that keeps the buggy first-per-resource behavior. Only one minimal root for_each test is added.

This uses the same approach as C2 and leaves the old FindImportStatements as unused code with the buggy semantics; it shares the per-resource parent-override gap, and its single root-module for_each test covers only the basic issue scenario.

Takes the same resource-level override approach as C2, with the same instance-level gap, and keeps a now-unused FindImportStatements wrapper that preserves the buggy semantics. Its tests are very thorough, covering both orderings, both locations and parent override.

It adds FindAllImportStatements, which fixes the same-module case, but it keeps the old FindImportStatements as an unused wrapper that still keeps only the first block per resource, and child imports for other instances are still silently dropped when a parent also imports into that resource; the order, location and count test matrix is solid.
